answer: Persistent-Operator Anchor Ledger. Each wallet links to a hardware-anchored operator key, and a shared operator's identities are mirrored in one ledger cluster. When any wallet in a cluster is caught sybiling, the ledger applies a penalty to the operator key: its anchor is throttled, raising per-identity resource cost. A violet flag marks the cluster publicly. Attacker cost: one throttled operator anchor per farm, not one cheap wallet.
